_comment: Live market data for the Forward OS / Forward Motion Freight portal. Feeds the dashboard Market Pulse card and the Rate Calculator's suggested-rate button. SCHEMA MUST MATCH the portal reader's BUILTIN_MARKET shape in app/src/App.jsx (mergeMarketData): asOf, blurb, dieselPerGal, spotAllIn, trend(up|down|flat), modality[{type,rpm,yoy}], lanes[{lane,rpm}], commodityRates{}. Missing/malformed fields fall back to builtin per-field. Maintained by Dex (market desk agent) — see _sourcing for what's live vs carried-forward. Deploys to forwardmotionfreight.com/market.json via GitHub Pages.
blurb: Diesel's turned back up — $6.352, two straight weekly gains and 17 cents off the low — so bump your fuel surcharge to the new index and keep your base linehaul firm. Northwest apple reefer loads are easing as trucks free up (Boston ~$12.2k, New York ~$11.8k), so quote off this week's board, not last month's.

_sourcing.status: EIGHTEENTH cycle with direct egress to the named sources blocked (WebFetch www.eia.gov, www.bluebookservices.com = getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND; curl eia.gov and indexbox.io = CONNECT tunnel 403; 20 other freight/fuel hosts probed with curl, all blocked). ONE CRACK FOUND: curl to s3.amazonaws.com (the barchart-news-store-prod USDA mirror) returns 200 and serves the raw USDA FVWTRK PDFs; text is extractable with plain python zlib (no PDF libs installed). That gave a PRIMARY USDA read for Yakima this cycle. WebSearch delivered EIA diesel for weeks ending 10/19 and 10/26 (secondary). asOf advanced 2026-10-16 -> 2026-10-26 on the strength of diesel 10/26 (headline number + trend) and USDA 10/20 Yakima; NOTE modality/commodity rates still reflect DAT week 42 (10/10-16) and spotAllIn is ~10/3 - see per-field notes. DAT week 43 (10/17-23) NOT found.
_sourcing.dieselPerGal: LIVE (medium confidence, secondary sources, arithmetic cross-checked). $6.352/gal for EIA week ending 2026-10-26, UP $0.076 from $6.276 (10/19), which was itself UP $0.097 from $6.179 (10/12). Sources: IndexBox write-up of the EIA weekly release via search summary (10/26 = $6.352, +7.6c w/w, ~$2.63 over year-ago; regular gasoline $4.269, -1.5c); Bluebook Services via search summary (EIA Oct. 20 update: +9.7c to $6.276, $2.66 over year-ago ~$3.62). Checks: 6.179+0.097=6.276 and 6.276+0.076=6.352 tie exactly; year-ago implied by 6.352-2.63 = ~$3.72 matches the independently reported EIA 10/27/2025 print (~$3.72). Series: $6.529 record (9/21) -> $6.382 -> $6.199 -> $6.179 (10/12 low) -> $6.276 (10/19) -> $6.352 (10/26). No primary EIA read (egress blocked). NOT USED: AAA/GasBuddy retail, FreightWaves DTS truck-stop index, all stale-year ($3-4) items, Bluebook 'nearly $6.30 AAA' retail mention.
_sourcing.trend: UP - two straight EIA diesel increases (+9.7c, +7.6c; +17.3c off the 10/12 low), flipping the prior DOWN call. Basis is the fuel move; DAT week 43 all-in rates not seen, but with diesel up they should be firming on fuel pass-through (not adjusted without a source). Counter-signal: USDA Yakima apple/pear loads easing w/w (see lanes) - regional, not national.
_sourcing.spotAllIn: CARRIED FORWARD, NOT re-verified (stale, ~10/3, now ~3.5 weeks). $3.53/mi, FreightWaves SONAR NTI (dry van incl. fuel) per FreightWaves 'Truckload's mixed signals' (published ~10/3-4). Re-searched this cycle: only undated NTI figures and an undated ~14% tender-rejection read surfaced; NTI daily is SONAR-subscription only. DAT does not publish a single blended national all-in; DAT per-equipment numbers (modality) were NOT blended into this field. Low-medium confidence; given diesel is now back UP ~17c since 10/12 the true all-in is probably not lower than this.
_sourcing.modality: Dry Van / Reefer / Flatbed UNCHANGED from last cycle (still LIVE as of DAT week 42 = Oct 10-16 2026, 7-day avg broker-to-carrier spot incl. fuel, via AJOT repost of the DAT release read through search summary): Dry Van $3.09, Reefer $3.66, Flatbed $3.64. Dry van linehaul $2.26 ex-fuel essentially flat. yoy (DAT linehaul): van +35%, reefer +33%, flatbed +29%. DAT week 43 (Oct 17-23) NOT found in searches - these are ONE WEEK STALE and need refresh; likely a touch higher on fuel pass-through, not adjusted without a source. REEFER STILL HAS NOT ROLLED OVER on the DAT all-in ($3.66, only -2c off the $3.68 peak, week 42). LTL (+12.5% GRI) and Intermodal ($1.39, -5%) CARRIED FORWARD, no new data.
_sourcing.commodityRates: In sync with modality (no reprice this cycle): General Dry Freight 3.09 (dry van), Frozen Seafood/Poultry 3.66 and Fresh Produce 3.66 (reefer), Coiled Steel 3.64 (flatbed). High-Value Electronics 2.60 carried forward, no data. NOTE: the app's FALLBACK_MARKET_RATES are older (2.47/3.20/3.20/3.57/2.60); only this live JSON overrides them.
_sourcing.lanes: Yakima, WA -> Northeast (reefer): PROMOTED, LIVE, PRIMARY SOURCE (high confidence). USDA AMS Specialty Crops 'National Truck Rate Report' FVWTRK dated Oct 21 2026, prices for Tuesday Oct 20 2026, Yakima Valley and Wenatchee District, apples and pears, parsed directly from the PDF via the s3 mirror. Boston: range $11,000-16,000, mostly $11,800-12,600 (midpoint $12,200), -4% w/w. New York: range $11,300-14,000, mostly $11,400-12,100 (midpoint $11,750), -7% w/w. Lane string uses the two midpoints ($11.8k-$12.2k). Truck availability moved from SHORTAGE (10/6, 10/13) to SLIGHT SHORTAGE (10/20) - Wenatchee/Yakima is loosening, rates easing off the highs (10/13: Boston mostly $11,800-13,500, New York $11,800-13,400). Other 10/20 destinations from Yakima, mostly: Atlanta $10,100-10,900 (-7%), Baltimore $11,200-12,000 (+1%), Philadelphia $10,800-11,600 (-3%), Miami $13,700-14,500 (0%), Chicago $8,200-8,900, Dallas $9,200-9,900, Los Angeles $3,600-4,000, Seattle $1,200-1,600. Prior carried value was the 9/29 reading ($12.6k-$12.7k midpoints). Atlanta -> Miami: CARRIED FORWARD, unchanged, 18 cycles - no origin-to-Miami absolute $/mi on a clean dated source (USDA FVWTRK Georgia origin covers tomatoes/okra to other cities, not this lane); NOT promoted. Memphis -> Atlanta: not searched, unchanged.
_sourcing.blurb: Rewritten around diesel turning back up ($6.352, two straight gains, +17c off the 10/12 low): reprice fuel surcharge to the index, hold base linehaul; and USDA-confirmed easing in Yakima apple loads as truck supply loosens (Boston ~$12.2k, NY ~$11.8k, -4%/-7% w/w).
_sourcing.directionalCaveatUnverified: (1) Diesel $6.352 (10/26) and $6.276 (10/19) rest on secondary search-summary reads (IndexBox, Bluebook), no primary EIA page; they tie arithmetically and to the year-ago comp, so confidence is medium. (2) DAT modality is week 42 (10/10-16), one week stale; week 43 not found. (3) spotAllIn $3.53 is ~10/3 and unrefreshed. (4) asOf 10/26 reflects diesel + Yakima; DAT modality is 10/16 and spotAllIn ~10/3 - revert asOf to 2026-10-16 if the badge should only advance with the DAT numbers. (5) Atlanta->Miami and Memphis->Atlanta ranges are old carried marketing-grade ranges.

refreshBlockers: Egress re-tested first: WebFetch to www.eia.gov and www.bluebookservices.com = getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND; curl to eia.gov and indexbox.io = 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403'; 20 other hosts probed with curl (fred.stlouisfed.org, api.eia.gov, logisticsmgmt.com, supplychain247.com, thetrucker.com, ajot.com, weeklydiesel.com, mondaydiesel.com, atlas.doe.gov, freightwaves.com, landline.media, ttnews.com, freshplaza.com, fleetowner.com, worktruckonline.com, finviz.com, etc.) all blocked. Delivered this cycle via that path: USDA Yakima->Boston/NY for Oct 20 (primary). Via WebSearch: EIA diesel 10/19 ($6.276) and 10/26 ($6.352).
